Estimate a search's false discovery proportion from its entrapment hits

stats_entrapment_fdp.Rd

Estimate the false discovery proportion among a search's discoveries from its entrapment hits, as a lower bound, a combined upper bound and a paired upper bound, at each of several q-value thresholds.

An entrapment experiment adds peptides that cannot be in the sample (from another species, or made from the target peptides) to the search database. Every entrapment the search reports is then a known false discovery, which lets you check the search's FDR claim instead of trusting it. mzLib's EntrapmentFdp.Sweep computes the three valid estimators of Wen et al. 2025 (the method FDRBench implements) at each q-value threshold:

Usage

stats_entrapment_fdp(targets, entrapments, ratio, thresholds = NULL, timeout = 600)

Arguments

targets

A TSV whose header names exactly score and q_value, in any order: one row per original-target candidate (precursor, peptide or protein group, whichever you are estimating for), decoys removed, each with its best q-value. Higher scores are better.

entrapments

A TSV whose header names score, q_value, partner_score and partner_q_value, and optionally foreign: one row per entrapment candidate. The partner columns copy the score and q-value of the one target this entrapment was made from, when the search identified it; leave both blank otherwise. foreign is 1 for an entrapment with no partner by construction (another species); blank or absent is mzLib's default, not foreign. Other columns are refused, so select these first.

ratio

r, the entrapment-to-target database size ratio (unitless). Required: mzLib has no default. paired is reported only when it is exactly 1, so for 1:1 pairing pass 1, not a ratio computed from database sizes after exclusions.

thresholds

The q-value thresholds to estimate at, as fractions (0.01 for 1%). Leave it NULL for mzLib's default sweep (0.001 to 0.100 in steps of 0.001 at mzLib d10017ce), echoed in thresholds.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

- lower_bound = N_E / (N_T + N_E). Above the FDR you claimed, the search fails to control it. Below, it proves nothing. - combined = N_E (1 + 1/r) / (N_T + N_E). An upper bound: at or below the claimed FDR, it is evidence of control. - paired: a tighter upper bound when each target has exactly one entrapment made from it (ratio = 1), using whether each discovered entrapment's own target was discovered too.

The "sample" estimator N_E / (r N_T) is invalid in both directions and is deliberately absent.

Value

An mzlibr_entrapment_fdp_estimates:

- records, a data.frame with one row per q-value threshold with a discovery: q_value_threshold (a q-value, fraction), where a candidate is discovered at or below it; target_count, N_T, targets discovered (discoveries); entrapment_count, N_E, entrapments discovered (discoveries); and three estimates of the false discovery proportion: lower_bound (fraction of discoveries), a lower bound (above your claimed FDR, the search fails to control it); combined (fraction of discoveries), an upper bound (at or below your claimed FDR, evidence of control; can exceed 1); and paired (fraction of discoveries), a tighter upper bound for 1:1 pairing (can exceed 1), NA where it does not apply: a ratio not exactly 1, or every entrapment foreign. - targets_file and entrapments_file, as absolute paths; ratio, r as you gave it (entrapment-to-target database size ratio, unitless); thresholds, the q-value thresholds estimated at, in order (yours or mzLib's default); thresholds_given; target_candidate_count and entrapment_candidate_count, the rows of the two files (candidates); foreign_count and partnered_count entrapments (candidates); threshold_count thresholds; empty_threshold_count, thresholds with no discoveries (thresholds), which have no row; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: what each estimate can and cannot show, plus any that apply to this input.

The input traps

Give one row per unit estimated, decoys removed, each with its best q-value: mzLib does not deduplicate, and it does not check a partner's copied score against the targets file. The k-fold paired estimator for k entrapments per target is not implemented.

Wraps

Wire verb stats entrapment-fdp. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.entrapment-fdp.yaml (bridge commit 60b1d25968a1) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • EntrapmentFdp.Sweep in mzLib/StatisticalModels/EntrapmentFdp.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • EntrapmentFdp.DefaultQValueThresholds in mzLib/StatisticalModels/EntrapmentFdp.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ScoredIdentification in mzLib/StatisticalModels/EntrapmentFdp.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • ScoredEntrapment in mzLib/StatisticalModels/EntrapmentFdp.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • EntrapmentFdpPoint in mzLib/StatisticalModels/EntrapmentFdp.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

targets

path; required. A TSV with a header row naming EXACTLY the columns score and q_value, in any order, then one row per original-target candidate (mzLib's ScoredIdentification): the unit you estimate the FDP of (precursor, peptide or protein group), decoys removed, each with its best q-value. score is the search's score, higher is better, on the same scale as the entrapments'; q_value is the q-value the search reported, a fraction. Every cell must be a finite number. Any other column is refused: select the two before writing the file.

entrapments

path; required. A TSV with a header row naming the columns score, q_value, partner_score and partner_q_value, and optionally foreign, in any order, then one row per entrapment candidate (mzLib's ScoredEntrapment). partner_score and partner_q_value are a COPY of the score and q-value of the one original target this entrapment was made from, when the search identified it; leave both blank (or NA) when it did not, when it cannot be resolved to one target, or when there is none. mzLib does not check them against the targets file. foreign is 1 or true for an entrapment with no target partner by construction (a foreign species), 0 or false otherwise; a blank cell, or no foreign column, is mzLib's default (ScoredEntrapment.IsForeign false). Any other column is refused, so a misspelt foreign column cannot fall back to the default.

ratio

float; in entrapment-to-target database size ratio (unitless); required; range > 0 and finite (mzLib's rule; anything else is mzLib's refusal, a usage error). r, the effective ratio of entrapment to target database size, used by the combined estimate. REQUIRED: mzLib has no default. paired is reported only when r is exactly 1: for 1:1 pairing give 1 itself, not a ratio computed from database sizes after exclusions (0.9998 drops it).

thresholds

float[]; in q-value (fraction, 0 to 1); default absent; range comma-separated finite numbers. The q-value thresholds to estimate at, comma-separated, in the order the rows should come in. A candidate is discovered at a threshold when its q-value is at or below it. Absent, the bridge sends mzLib's EntrapmentFdp.DefaultQValueThresholds (0.001, 0.002, ..., 0.100, each i/1000, at d10017ce) and echoes them.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

targets_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the targets table.

entrapments_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the entrapments table.

ratio

float; in entrapment-to-target database size ratio (unitless); never NA. r, as given.

thresholds

float[]; in q-value (fraction, 0 to 1); never NA. The thresholds estimated at, in order: the --thresholds given, or mzLib's default.

thresholds_given

bool; never NA. True when --thresholds was given; false when thresholds is mzLib's DefaultQValueThresholds.

target_candidate_count

int; in candidates; never NA. Rows read from the targets file.

entrapment_candidate_count

int; in candidates; never NA. Rows read from the entrapments file.

foreign_count

int; in candidates; never NA. Entrapments marked foreign.

partnered_count

int; in candidates; never NA. Entrapments with a partner.

threshold_count

int; in thresholds; never NA. The length of thresholds.

empty_threshold_count

int; in thresholds; never NA. Thresholds at which nothing was discovered, where every estimate is 0/0, so mzLib leaves them out of the table.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. threshold_count - empty_threshold_count.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per threshold with a discovery, in thresholds order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Five static caveats, plus one each when a threshold had no discoveries, when paired is null at every threshold (with the ratio and the foreign count), and when no entrapment has a partner.

Columns of records

q_value_threshold

float; in q-value (fraction, 0 to 1); never NA. The threshold.

target_count

int; in discoveries; never NA. N_T: targets with a q-value at or below the threshold.

entrapment_count

int; in discoveries; never NA. N_E: entrapments with a q-value at or below the threshold.

lower_bound

float; in fraction of discoveries (an FDP estimate); never NA. Eq. 2, N_E / (N_T + N_E). A lower bound on the FDP: above the claimed FDR, it shows the search fails to control it; below, it shows nothing.

combined

float; in fraction of discoveries (an FDP estimate; can exceed 1); never NA. Eq. 1, N_E (1 + 1/r) / (N_T + N_E). An upper bound: at or below the claimed FDR, it is evidence of control. Not capped at 1.

paired

float; in fraction of discoveries (an FDP estimate; can exceed 1); NA when does not apply: the ratio is not exactly 1, or every entrapment is foreign. Eq. 4, (N_E + N_{E>=s>T} + 2 N_{E>T>=s}) / (N_T + N_E): a tighter upper bound for 1:1 pairing. N_{E>=s>T} counts discovered entrapments whose partner was not discovered (no partner counts so); N_{E>T>=s} those whose partner was discovered but ranked behind them, by lower q-value and then higher score, an exact tie counting the entrapment ahead. Not capped at 1.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

targets or entrapments missing, blank or not found; a table empty; a header with an empty, repeated, missing or unknown column (each named); a row whose field count differs from its header; a score or q_value that is not a finite number; a partner with a score but no q-value or the reverse, or not finite; a foreign cell other than 0, 1, true, false or blank

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--ratio absent, without a value or not a number; --thresholds without a value, empty, or with an entry that is not a finite number

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the ratio (its ArgumentOutOfRangeException, reclassified): not a positive finite number

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Wen et al. 2025, as FDRBench implements it. lower_bound can only show that a search fails to control its FDR; combined is an upper bound, evidence that it does; paired is a tighter upper bound for 1:1 pairing. None is capped at 1.

  • A candidate is discovered when its q-value is at or below the threshold, and a partner by its own q-value. A discovered pair is ranked lower q-value first, then higher score, and an exact tie counts against the search.

  • Give one row per unit estimated (precursor, peptide or protein group), decoys removed, each with its best q-value: mzLib does not deduplicate. A partner's score and q-value are copies of its target's row, and mzLib does not check them.

  • paired is reported only for a ratio of exactly 1 with some entrapment not foreign. The sample estimator N_E / (r N_T), invalid in both directions, is deliberately absent (mzLib), and the k-fold paired estimator for k entrapments per target is not implemented.

  • An entrapment generator's exclusions change the inputs in opposite directions (mzLib's EntrapmentFdp.ClassifyExclusion): an entrapment that is really a target peptide comes out of the entrapments file; a target that cannot be traced to one target stays in the targets file but is nobody's partner.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::entrapment_fdp_with with EntrapmentFdpOptions

Since

References

  • doi:10.1038/s41592-025-02719-x: the lower-bound (eq. 2), combined (eq. 1) and paired (eq. 4) entrapment estimators mzLib implements, and why the sample estimator is invalid (Wen et al., Nat Methods 22:1454, 2025; the method FDRBench implements)

Examples


# mzLib's own hand-built search (seven targets, four entrapments, one for each case the paired
# estimate distinguishes), checked against the entrapment project's reference script:
data <- system.file("extdata", "stats", package = "mzLibR")
fdp <- stats_entrapment_fdp(file.path(data, "entrapment_reference_targets.tsv"),
  file.path(data, "entrapment_reference_entrapments.tsv"), ratio = 1)
fdp
#> <mzlibr_entrapment_fdp_estimates> 7 targets, 4 entrapments, ratio 1, 100 of 100 thresholds with a discovery
fdp$records[fdp$records$q_value_threshold == 0.01, ]
#>    q_value_threshold target_count entrapment_count lower_bound  combined
#> 10              0.01            4                3   0.4285714 0.8571429
#>       paired
#> 10 0.8571429
